note:
THE DRIVER TEST SUITE IS 295 s AND ESSENTIALLY ALL OF IT IS REDUNDANT GENESIS. Measured today on ambrose, dev profile, box otherwise idle. Nathan noticed a driver- test binary pegging a single core during a clients phase and asked whether it could be made concurrent. It is ALREADY concurrent; that is not the lever.

  cargo build --manifest-path clients/game/bin/Cargo.toml --tests     27.3 s
  the whole driver test binary       295.2 s wall, 670% CPU, 25 tests
  ONE test, isolated                  50.4 s wall,  81% CPU

670% means ~6.7 tests already run at once. The single pegged core is the TAIL -- the last long test finishing alone. Adding parallelism buys nothing: the suite is work-bound, not thread-bound.

WHERE THE WORK GOES. `Driver::start(seed, target)` calls `build_world`, and there are 34 call sites in the bin crate -- 28 in tests/driver.rs alone -- of which 32 use SEED 42. The same world, rebuilt ~28 times per run. One test in isolation is 50.4 s at 81% CPU, single-threaded, doing exactly one genesis. Genesis is not a component of the cost; it is the cost.

THE SEAM ALREADY EXISTS, one function below it:

  pub fn start_from_world(world: World, target: PossessTarget) -> Result<Driver, DriverError>

Its own doc: "Everything Driver::start does EXCEPT building the world", and "a caller that has just paid ~2.2 s for one pays nothing again here". It exists because The Overture (ruling R5) moved genesis to a worker thread, and Task 8's world cache needed the same shape.

THE CHANGE: build seed 42 once per test binary, clone per test, call start_from_world. World is { seed, registry, ledger } -- plain data -- and derives Clone. The committed seed-42 world is 5.3 MB, so a memcpy against a 50 s genesis is not a close call.

PRECEDENT IN THE SIBLING CRATE: The Quire did exactly this for hornvale-game-core, committing seed-42 session fixtures so tests read a world instead of paying for one. The split there is by WHAT A TEST NEEDS, not unit-vs-integration. This is the same move for game/bin.

TWO THINGS I DID NOT VERIFY, and they are the ones that decide the design:
  - whether World is auto Send + Sync, which a `static OnceLock<World>` needs. It
    looks like plain data but I did not compile the assertion.
  - the actual clone cost. I am asserting it is negligible against 50 s from the
    5.3 MB figure, which is an inference, not a measurement.

I am NOT taking this. It is a change to clients/game/bin while campaigns are actively landing there, and the measurement is worth more than my guess at the patch. Whoever owns that crate should size it against the two unknowns above. If it lands, the honest expectation is one genesis plus 25 clones -- somewhere in the 3-5x range, and worth re-measuring rather than quoting me.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE SUITE: the `clients` phase runs on every stage gate and every merge. At ~1300-1900 s per chamber job tonight, ~295 s of this is one suite rebuilding one world 28 times.
